belongs_to: Opening text of 1.1: 'The symbol on this signboard needs to be recreated on another board. How do we do it?'
description: Coloured illustration of a signboard: a square-ish rounded rectangle with a thick black border and a pale blue-grey inside, fixed on top of a vertical post striped in blue and white/grey, standing in grass with two small yellow-green flowers. Inside the board is ONE thin black check-mark symbol (a short stroke from upper left down to a bottom corner, then a long stroke from that corner up to the upper right; the angle between the two strokes looks about 90 degrees). No letters, no lengths, no angle values are printed on it. Only the check-mark symbol carries mathematical content; board, post and grass are scenery.
unclear: The board and post art is decoration; only the check-mark symbol is the working content (the same symbol is redrawn bare with corner points A, B, C in P01-shape-1).

belongs_to: 'Let us name the corner points of this symbol as shown.' and 'Are the arm lengths AB and BC sufficient to exactly recreate this figure?'
description: The check-mark symbol alone on white, drawn as two black line segments meeting at a bottom corner. Three labelled points: A at the free end of the SHORT arm (upper left), B at the corner/vertex at the bottom, C at the free end of the LONG arm (upper right, at about the same height as A, slightly higher). AB is the short arm, BC the long arm (BC is about twice AB). Angle at B looks about 90 degrees. No lengths, no angle value, no tick marks or arcs are printed. Point letters are small serif capitals placed beside the end points.
unclear: Angle at B is not printed; measured on the page it is roughly 90 degrees.

belongs_to: 'Suppose these lengths are AB = 4 cm, BC = 8 cm. We observe that several such symbols can be constructed with the same lengths.'
description: A row of FOUR check-mark symbols side by side, each a pair of black segments AB (short) and BC (long, about twice AB) meeting at B at the bottom; each labelled A (free end of the short arm, upper left), B (bottom vertex), C (free end of the long arm). All four have the same two arm lengths but a different angle at B, so C sits at a different place. From left to right: (1) angle ABC about 90 degrees, C up and to the right at moderate height; (2) angle about 65 degrees, BC steeper, C higher; (3) angle about 50 degrees, BC very steep, C far above (highest of the four, almost over B); (4) angle about 97 degrees (widest), BC nearly flat rising gently to the right, C at the far right and only slightly above B. AB points up-left in all four at the same slope. No lengths, angles or marks are printed on the figure; only the letters A, B, C under/beside the points.
unclear: Angle values are not printed; the angles given (about 90, 65, 50, 97 degrees) are measured by eye/pixels from the page and are approximate.

belongs_to: 'Figures that are exact copies of each other ... are said to be congruent. Congruent figures can be superimposed exactly, one over the other.'
description: Two coloured cut-out pictures side by side. Left: a flat pink (mauve) square-ish shape whose four corners are each cut away by a concave quarter-circle arc (notched corners), thin dark outline, slight shadow. Right: the same pink shape lying in a slanted, perspective view (like a tilted parallelogram with the same notched corners), with a pale cream/beige translucent copy of the same shape laid over it, shifted slightly up and to the right, so a thin strip of pink shows along the lower left and bottom edge. It shows tracing paper / cut-out superimposed on the pink figure. No labels or numbers.

belongs_to: 'Two congruent figures are shown below. You could use a tracing paper to trace the first figure and superimpose it on the second one.'
description: Two identical plain white outline shapes side by side, same size, same orientation. Each is a circle with its upper-right quarter (one quadrant) cut away: the outline runs from the top of the circle straight down a vertical radius to the centre, then along a horizontal radius to the right-most point of the circle, then round the remaining three quarters of the circle (left, bottom) back to the top. Black outline, no fill, no labels or numbers.

belongs_to: 'Note that while checking for congruence, a figure can be rotated or flipped ... So, the following pairs of figures are also congruent' (first pair, top of p.3)
description: A pair of identical bent-strip (corner bracket) shapes, plain outline, no labels. LEFT piece: a corner at the upper left made of a horizontal strip along the top and a vertical strip down the left side; the right end of the horizontal strip is cut at a slant (cut runs from the top outer corner down and to the left) and the bottom end of the vertical strip is cut at a slant. RIGHT piece: the same bracket turned through a half turn (180 degrees): corner at the lower right, a horizontal strip along the bottom and a vertical strip up the right side, with the slanted ends at the left end of the bottom strip and the top end of the right strip. Both pieces have the same strip width (about one fifth of the arm length) and the same arm lengths. The pieces are placed apart (left piece upper left, right piece lower right of it).

belongs_to: '... the following pairs of figures are also congruent' (second pair, top of p.3)
description: A pair of half-discs (semicircles) with a gap between them, plain outline, no labels. LEFT: a semicircle whose straight edge is vertical and on its RIGHT side (curved side on the left, like a bracket opening to the right). RIGHT: a semicircle whose straight edge is vertical and on its LEFT side (curved side on the right, like the letter D). The straight edges face each other with a small gap (about a fifth of the width of one half-disc); the two halves are mirror images of each other (flipped) and the same size.

belongs_to: Figure it Out Q1: 'Check if the two figures are congruent.'
description: Two check-mark symbols (like the signboard symbol) side by side, each two black line segments meeting at a bottom corner: a short arm rising to the upper left and a long arm rising to the upper right (long arm about twice the short arm). No letters, lengths or angle values printed. LEFT figure: angle between the arms about 90 degrees (long arm rises at a moderate slope). RIGHT figure: the arms have the same lengths as the left figure but the angle at the bottom corner is smaller, about 72 degrees (the short arm leans less, the long arm rises more steeply). The right figure is placed slightly higher and to the right of the left one.

belongs_to: Figure it Out Q2: 'Circle the pairs that appear congruent.'
description: Four pairs of plain black outline shapes in a 2 x 2 arrangement (two pairs on top, two below), no labels or numbers. TOP-LEFT: two identical teardrop shapes of the same size; the left one has its point at the top (tip up, slightly to the right), the right one is the same teardrop turned about a quarter turn so its point is at the left. TOP-RIGHT: two cloud outlines; the left cloud is larger, lumpy with about 4 bumps along the top, tilted slightly; the right cloud is smaller and flatter with a different bump pattern (similar in style but a different size and outline). BOTTOM-LEFT: two jagged starburst (explosion) shapes; the left is smaller (about 11 spikes) and the right is larger (about 11 spikes, about 1.5 times as wide); same style, different sizes. BOTTOM-RIGHT: two leaf-pair shapes; each is a tall upright pointed leaf and a second pointed leaf lying nearly horizontal, both joined at their lower end; in the left pair the lying leaf extends to the LEFT, in the right pair it extends to the RIGHT, so the right pair is the mirror image of the left pair (same size).
unclear: Spike counts of the two starbursts were counted on an enlargement (about 11 each) and may be off by one.
Cloud pair: outlines are similar in style but not identical; exact bump counts not verified.

belongs_to: Figure it Out Q4: 'How would we check if two figures like the one below are congruent?'
description: One plain black line figure (no labels, no numbers) made of two straight segments forming a Y-like shape: one LONG straight segment running from the upper right down to the lower left, and one SHORTER segment that comes from the upper left and ends exactly on the long segment (it meets it at a point that splits the long segment into an upper part of about 55% and a lower part of about 45%). unclear: No measurements are printed on the figure; the proportions are measured from the page and approximate.

belongs_to: Figure it Out Q4: 'Use this to identify whether each of the following pairs are congruent.'

unclear: The four figures measure identical on the page; whether the book intends the pairs to be rows or columns, and whether any pair is meant to differ, is not visible. Check the printed answer.

belongs_to: Start of 1.2 Congruence of Triangles: 'Meera and Rabia have been asked to make a cardboard cutout identical to a triangular frame they have in school.'

No dimensions, letters or marks are printed on the picture; the side lengths 40 cm, 60 cm, 80 cm appear only in the text on p.5.

belongs_to: Rabia's construction: 'draw a line segment ... 6 cm, and then draw circles from each of its end points with radii 4 cm and 8 cm. But the circles would intersect at two points, forming two triangles: triangle ABE and triangle ABF.'
description: A horizontal solid segment AB with A on the left and B on the right, labelled 'AB = 6 cm' (the text sits just below the segment, inside the small circle). Two DASHED circles: a small circle with centre A (radius 4 cm, which is two thirds of AB) and a large circle with centre B (radius 8 cm, which is 4/3 of AB); the large circle is much bigger and extends far to the right of B, and its left part passes just left of A. The two circles cross at two points E (upper) and F (lower), both slightly to the left of A and directly above/below each other. Solid segments AE, AF, BE and BF are drawn, so two triangles ABE (above AB) and ABF (below AB) are shown, mirror images of each other in line AB. Labels: A (just left of A's point), B, E (above the upper intersection), F (below the lower intersection) and 'AB = 6 cm'. The radii 4 cm and 8 cm are NOT written on the figure.

belongs_to: 'Conventions to Express Congruence': 'The two triangles given below are congruent. How can these two triangles be superimposed? Which vertices of triangle XYZ and triangle ABC should we overlap?'

Triangle ABC (left): C at the top left, A at the bottom left (a little to the right of C), B at the bottom right; AC is the left side, AB the short bottom side, CB the long slanting side. Tick marks: AC has ONE tick, AB has TWO ticks, CB (the long side) has THREE ticks. Triangle XYZ (right, turned): X at the top, Z at the far right, Y at the bottom left; XZ has ONE tick, XY has TWO ticks, YZ (the long side) has THREE ticks. So AC=XZ (1 tick), AB=XY (2 ticks), BC=YZ (3 ticks). No lengths or angles printed.

belongs_to: 'To capture this relation ... their congruence is written as follows: triangle ABC congruent to triangle XYZ' (colour-coded correspondence diagram)

The arrowheads point at X, Y and Z.
